learned_rules.situation: When required output fields are completely missing but the agent produced some output (like system prompts or other content)
learned_rules.reason: A.8 (Downstream_Handoff_Failure) explicitly covers cases where 'Agent output lacks critical information, proper structure, or necessary formatting' and the overlap guidance states A.8 applies to 'structural/format compliance' issues with 'complete sentences but missing fields/malformed structure'
learned_rules.not_code: Don't use A.5 (Output_Truncation) unless there's clear evidence of mid-sentence cutoff or token limit truncation. A.5 is for incomplete generation, not improperly structured but complete generation.

learned_rules.situation: When an error involves failing to complete a specified number of retrieval hops in a multi-hop task (e.g., 0 out of 3 required hops performed)
learned_rules.reason: B.9 specifically addresses 'stopping the retrieval chain before completing all required hops in a multi-hop task.' When the error explicitly mentions a multi-hop requirement (e.g., 'three-hop retrieval task', 'exactly three retrievals') that was not met, this is the coordinator's failure to execute the hop sequence, not the solver's evidence analysis failure.
learned_rules.not_code: Don't confuse with B.2, which applies when the solver DOES analyze evidence but fails to recognize it's insufficient. B.2 is for poor evidence evaluation; B.9 is for incomplete multi-hop execution. The distinguishing factor: if the description emphasizes 'X-hop task' and 'Y hops completed where Y < X', use B.9.

learned_rules.situation: When agent output shows template/structure elements but lacks actual generated content
learned_rules.reason: The taxonomy distinguishes A.7 as 'information provided upstream but lost during processing' versus A.8 as 'information may be present but not formatted/structured for downstream systems.' Empty template fields indicate the agent failed at the output formatting stage (processing→output), not that it lost input information (input→processing).
learned_rules.not_code: Don't use A.7 unless there's evidence that specific information was provided in input but disappeared during processing. Empty output templates are A.8 downstream handoff failures.

disambiguation_rules.A.2|A.5: A.2 shows system-level resource errors (OOM, context window warnings) in logs. A.5 shows max token generation limits reached without memory/resource errors. If output stops AND there are memory/context errors, use A.2. If output stops at token limit without resource errors, use A.5.
disambiguation_rules.A.1|A.3: A.1 shows explicit timeout signals (SIGTERM, SIGKILL) or timeout error messages with time limits. A.3 shows generic exceptions/stack traces without time-related signals. Check logs for timeout-specific vs. other error types.
disambiguation_rules.A.2|A.3: A.2 specifically shows resource-related errors (OOM, context window exceeded). A.3 shows other system errors (uncaught exceptions, generic error codes). Look for resource metrics in error messages.
disambiguation_rules.A.11|A.7: A.11: Retrieved passages themselves are demonstrably insufficient/irrelevant (inspect retrieval system output directly). A.7: Retrieved passages contain needed info but agent didn't use it (compare retrieval results vs. agent's processing). If passages are empty/bad, use A.11. If passages are good but unused, use A.7.
disambiguation_rules.A.10|A.7: A.10 is specific to multi-hop scenarios where degradation occurs across iterations (temporal pattern of information loss). A.7 applies to single-stage or initial information loss. Check if failure occurs within one stage (A.7) or progressively across multiple hops (A.10).
disambiguation_rules.A.3|A.4: A.4 shows explicit natural language refusal statements ('I cannot', 'I will not', safety declinations). A.3 shows system errors (exceptions, error codes). A.4 is intentional/policy-based; A.3 is unintentional system failure. Check for human-readable refusal text vs. technical error messages.
disambiguation_rules.A.5|A.8: A.5: Output cuts off mid-generation (incomplete sentences/structures) due to token limits. A.8: Output may be complete in length but missing specific required fields/formatting for downstream consumption. A.5 is about generation truncation; A.8 is about structural/format compliance. If mid-sentence cutoff with token limit, use A.5. If complete sentences but missing fields/malformed structure, use A.8.
disambiguation_rules.A.7|A.8: A.7: Information was provided upstream but lost during agent processing (input→processing failure). A.8: Information may be present but not formatted/structured for downstream systems (processing→output failure). Check if input contained the info (A.7) vs. output structure issues (A.8).
disambiguation_rules.A.10|A.6: A.6: Exact textual repetition (same sentences/paragraphs repeated). A.10: Logical inconsistency or forgetting across hops without exact repetition. A.6 is syntactic repetition; A.10 is semantic degradation. Look for copy-paste repetition (A.6) vs. contradictory reasoning (A.10).
disambiguation_rules.A.10|A.2: A.2: Context window resource constraint causes information loss (system error logs). A.10: Information degradation despite adequate resources (no resource errors). Check for context window exceeded errors (A.2) vs. logical inconsistency without resource errors (A.10).
disambiguation_rules.B.2|B.3: B.2: Solver doesn't acknowledge the evidence gaps at all (no meta-analysis of evidence sufficiency). B.3: Solver may acknowledge gaps but still renders definitive SUPPORTS/REFUTES verdict anyway. If the solver explicitly discusses evidence completeness but proceeds with verdict = B.3. If solver ignores evidence analysis entirely = B.2.
disambiguation_rules.B.3|B.9: B.3: Solver-level issue - makes definitive verdict on available (but insufficient) evidence. B.9: Coordinator-level issue - stops requesting more hops/retrieval when multi-hop chain is incomplete. Check who triggers conclusion: if Solver renders verdict = B.3, if Coordinator stops requesting hops = B.9.
disambiguation_rules.B.1|B.5: B.1: Ambiguity in task specification (what to verify, how to judge, inconsistent requirements). B.5: Ambiguity specifically in retrieval guidance (what to search for, which entities to query). If the problem affects verification criteria/task definition = B.1. If problem affects search query formation = B.5.
disambiguation_rules.B.1|B.4: B.4: Specifically about compound claims with multiple independent facts lacking decomposition guidance (observable: claim has AND/OR structure, multiple verifiable components). B.1: General ambiguity/inconsistency in task specification. If claim clearly has 2+ independent facts without decomposition = B.4. If single claim but instructions are unclear/varying = B.1.
disambiguation_rules.B.6|B.7: B.6: Misreading what passage explicitly states (claims passage says X when it says Y). B.7: Failure to recognize contradiction between passage and claim (passage says NOT-X, claim says X, but solver doesn't flag conflict). Check if error is about reading comprehension (B.6) vs. comparison/contradiction detection (B.7).
disambiguation_rules.B.2|B.9: B.2: Solver fails to analyze evidence sufficiency (doesn't discuss gaps). B.9: Coordinator stops retrieval chain early (doesn't request more hops). Check the agent: Solver's analysis lacking = B.2, Coordinator stops hop sequence = B.9. Also check if it's multi-hop specific (B.9) or general evidence analysis (B.2).
disambiguation_rules.B.2|B.7: B.7: Evidence actively contradicts claim but solver doesn't detect it (passages present, contradiction missed). B.2: Evidence is insufficient/incomplete but solver doesn't analyze sufficiency (passages absent/incomplete, gap not acknowledged). If relevant passages exist but contradict = B.7. If passages missing/incomplete = B.2.
disambiguation_rules.C.1|C.4: C.1 is specific to multi-hop chains where identifiable entities/relationships are skipped (e.g., missing 'person→work→person' links). C.4 is broader and includes any invalid logical inference, contradictions, or non-sequiturs. If the missing piece is a specific entity-relationship hop, use C.1. If it's a general logical fallacy or contradiction, use C.4.
disambiguation_rules.C.3|C.4: C.3 specifically involves structural decomposition of compound claims (AND/OR confusion, missing conjuncts). C.4 is about invalid inference patterns. If you can point to 'this is an AND statement but only one part was checked,' use C.3. If the error is in the inference logic itself (non-sequitur, contradiction), use C.4.
disambiguation_rules.C.1|C.7: C.7 is about entity identity confusion (same entity treated as different, or vice versa). C.1 is about missing logical connection steps in a chain. If the issue is 'didn't recognize entity A and entity B are the same,' use C.7. If it's 'skipped the intermediate relationship between A and C,' use C.1.
disambiguation_rules.C.5|C.7: C.5 is specifically about work-author/creator confusion (treating title as author or vice versa). C.7 is general entity coreference (any entity identity confusion). If it involves work vs. creator confusion, use C.5. For other entity identity issues, use C.7.
disambiguation_rules.C.11|C.2: C.2 is specifically existential/universal quantifier confusion ('some' vs 'all'/'none'). C.11 is about set membership and subset relationships. If the error involves quantifier confusion (treating 'exists one' as 'all' or vice versa), use C.2. If it's about category membership or subset logic, use C.11.
disambiguation_rules.C.6|C.8: C.6 is specifically temporal (dates, years, time periods). C.8 is general comparative reasoning (any quantitative/qualitative comparison). If it involves time calculations, use C.6. For other magnitude comparisons, use C.8.
disambiguation_rules.C.10|C.4: C.10 is specifically about conditional logic errors (affirming consequent, denying antecedent, confusing necessary/sufficient). C.4 is general logical reasoning errors. If you can identify a specific conditional logic fallacy pattern, use C.10. Otherwise, use C.4.
disambiguation_rules.C.12|C.4: C.12 is specifically about causal reasoning (correlation vs causation, reversed causality). C.4 is general logical errors. If the claim or reasoning explicitly involves causation ('X caused Y'), use C.12. For other logical inference errors, use C.4.
disambiguation_rules.C.4|C.9: C.9 is specifically about negation being ignored, misscoped, or double-applied (look for 'not', 'no', 'none', etc.). C.4 is general logical errors. If the error involves mishandling explicit negation markers, use C.9. Otherwise, use C.4.
disambiguation_rules.C.2|C.3: C.3 is about structural decomposition (AND vs OR, missing conjuncts in compound claims). C.2 is about quantifier scope (existential vs universal). If it's about 'claim has parts X AND Y but only checked X,' use C.3. If it's about 'found one example and concluded universal claim,' use C.2.
